summary: GRE rewrite at customer edge causing gRPC keepalive probes to be dropped and streaming disconnects in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer running Redwood Private (VPC peered, on-prem edge) reports intermittent streaming disconnects and control-plane heartbeat delays. Symptom window is ~5-30 minutes of normal activity then long-lived gRPC streams abruptly stall and fail to recover without a full reconnect. TLS sessions for model shard downloads also observed to reset in the same time window.

Impact:
- Customer-facing production traffic experiences streaming failures and occasional model download errors, causing degraded UX for real-time features.
- Affects a subset of serving nodes behind customer on-prem edge (GRE tunnel + NAT) not seen in hosted deployments.

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployed in customer VPC peered via TGW to on-prem edge.
- Customer edge uses GRE tunnel to forward traffic into corporate network with an intermediate translation appliance that rewrites outer headers and performs connection tracking.
- Affected nodes: serving pool siphoned through that GRE path (prod-us-east-1).

Observed timing: starts ~2026-03-04 22:15 UTC and recurs several times each hour when idle periods exceed ~90s.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Establish long-lived gRPC streaming session to a model route from a client behind the customer edge.
2) Leave the stream idle for ~90-150 seconds while heartbeats/keepalives run at default (client 60s, server ~120s).
3) Observe retransmits from client and eventual stream failure with gRPC status UNAVAILABLE or ECONNRESET, requiring full reconnect.
4) For control-plane tests, perform repeated presigned S3 range downloads over same path and watch for TLS session resets during same time windows.
logs:
tcpdump excerpt (serving node side):
- Repeated TCP keepalive probes from client (SEQ=..., ACK=...), followed by multiple retransmissions.
- Final sequence shows RST from intermediate appliance with no corresponding FIN.
- conntrack logs on customer edge show ephemeral mapping timeout fired with reason 'ASSURED' around the same timestamps.
TLS logs:
- Client TLS session resumptions fail with 'alert unknown_ca' not relevant; primary observed artifact is session reset following transport reset.
(Full pcap and conntrack dump uploaded to customer case bucket: s3://redwood-support/docuscale-145678/pcap_20260304.tar.gz)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: MTU or TCP offload causing large frame fragmentation leading to retransmits. TCP MSS and PMTU checks did not show fragmentation at datalink layer between AWS and customer edge.
Second hypothesis: stateful appliance in GRE path is rewriting fields in a way that breaks end-to-end 5-tuple hashing, leading to asymmetric egress for retransmits and conntrack entry churn.

Collected evidence: conntrack timeouts aligned with stream drop times; tcpdump at two points (serving node + customer edge) show keepalive probes arriving at edge but retransmits returned on a different outer source IP, causing appliance to discard the packets and issue RST to internal host.

Reproduced in lab by replicating GRE + NAT rewrite: enabling address-rewrite on test appliance produced identical keepalive loss pattern. Disabling rewrite prevented retransmit misattribution and streams remained healthy across >30 minutes of idle time.
Correlation: incidents only occur when GRE tunnel is configured to rewrite outer source IP and reassign ephemeral ports (policy present on customer's transit appliance).
comments: 2026-03-05 - Support (Maya Chen): Customer reports intermittent stream stalls affecting ~7% of requests. Attached pcap and conntrack log. Asking for escalation to networking/SRE.

2026-03-05 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): I can reproduce with a test appliance. Hypothesis: GRE outer-rewrite + ephemeral port reassign is causing asymmetric path for retransmits. Need customer to test disabling rewrite or preserve original tuple.
2026-03-05 - Customer (DocuScale network ops - Ryan Patel): We can toggle the policy during a maintenance window. Asking for precise config steps and expected behavior.

2026-03-06 - Support (Diego Alvarez): Provided lab-tested checklist: 1) disable outer-source rewrite on GRE transit appliance OR enable 'preserve-5tuple' mode; 2) lower keepalive interval as short-term workaround (client tcp_keepalive 30s); 3) increase conntrack timeout to avoid churn. Also linked runbook and PR for diagnostic tooling.
2026-03-06 - Customer (Ryan Patel): Applied 'preserve-5tuple' config to GRE appliance in canary VPC. Observed zero streaming disconnects over 6 hours. Rolling to prod now.
2026-03-07 - Support (Maya Chen): Confirmed with customer that incidents stopped after config change. Closing ticket and adding follow-up action for runbook updates.
resolution: Root cause: customer transit appliance was configured to rewrite the outer GRE source IP and reassign ephemeral ports for flow aggregation. This broke end-to-end 5-tuple preservation for retransmitted keepalive packets, which caused the appliance to misattribute retransmits and inject RSTs toward the serving nodes. Workarounds/fix applied: customer enabled 'preserve-5tuple' / disabled outer-source rewrite on GRE appliance. Short-term mitigations: decreased client keepalive interval and increased conntrack timeouts to reduce probability of mapping churn. Long-term follow-up: added guidance to Private deployment runbook (linked) and support diagnostic script (PR #88) to detect 5-tuple rewriting in customer paths. Ticket resolved after 24 hours of clean telemetry post-change.
follow_up_actions: Add GRE/translation checks to Private onboarding checklist (owner: Onboarding team)
Publish KB article: 'GRE tunnels and long-lived gRPC streams' with configuration examples (owner: Docs)
Add automated diag in support toolbox to flag 5-tuple rewrite signatures (owner: SRE)
Customer asked for a 30-day check-in to confirm no regressions (owner: CSM)
